verdictBasis: 1 blocker, 4 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT was gated at 0 and 0.
verdictStatement: Every repair this successor claims, it made — and the two hardest ones it made well. The trust-store reservation is not a placeholder: it states why each of the three candidate classes is wrong, which is a better answer than an assignment would have been. The v1→v2 path is the cleanest succession I have measured in this corpus: 117 changed leaf paths, every one on the declared roster, 61 of 61 non-roster paths byte-identical, reviewGuidance a pure append. I attacked the roster claim directly and could not dent it. The blocker is not a repair that failed. It is that the repair was applied to one of two identical bounds. v1's defect was assigning the grant journal into SC-OPS over an owner-recorded 'not a grant journal' bar without citing it. v2 finds that bar in DR-005, cites it properly, and supersedes it by name — and does not find the identical bar in DR-002's preview disposition, which is equally owner-recorded, equally pinned in the live file 08 row, and carries the same six words. So SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL is a correctly-built supersession of half its subject matter, and the placement it authorizes still lands on a live bound nobody has named.

blockers.whyBlocker: This is v1's CLAUDE-V1-B1 surviving on a second row. The subject's own statement of the defect is exact — /proposedSupersession/whyNotSilent reads 'v1 assigned the journal to SC-OPS without citing D-060. That is the defect. This generation cites the bound and names the supersession.' Measured against that standard, v2 still assigns the journal into SC-OPS without citing D-058. A coordinator recording SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL would reasonably read /proposedSupersession/of as the complete list of contrary bounds being displaced; it is not, so the recording would leave a live owner-recorded bar standing against the very placement it authorizes. P-002-4 also supplies the completeness standard this row is measured by — 'must assign every persisted byte one class, owner, writer, and lifecycle before blueprint work' — which makes its absence from the input set doubly consequential.
blockers.theNarrowReadingAndWhyItDoesNotSave: In fairness: P-002-4's surface is qualified 'for the non-semantic invocation/audit envelope', which is narrower than P-005-2's whole-class surface. A reader could argue P-002-4 bars only the envelope from BEING a grant journal, and that a separately-placed journal in the same class does not violate it. I do not think that reading rescues the artifact, and it does not change the repair: under the narrow reading the bound still needs citing and expressly dispositioning ('P-002-4 is not superseded because its surface is the envelope, not the class'), and under the broad reading it needs adding to /proposedSupersession/of. Either way the current bytes are silent, and silence about a live owner-recorded bound is the exact defect this generation exists to cure.
blockers.notARequestToUnassign: As at v1, I am not asking for the journal to return to UNASSIGNED. The assignment is the right direction and the supersession machinery around it is well built. The defect is coverage, not concept.
blockers.minimumRepair: Add route-b.DR-002.preview-disposition.v2.json (301ea338…) and D-058 to /recordedInputs/governingSources. Then either add 'P-002-4 not-a-grant-journal bound' to /proposedSupersession/of and the DR-002 recording owner to ownersWhoseConcurrenceIsRequired, or record in /proposedSupersession an express finding that P-002-4's envelope-scoped surface is not displaced, with the reasoning stated.
blockers.theSweepIsClosedEnded: I ran the sweep I would otherwise have recommended, so the coordinator does not have to. Case-sensitive search for the phrase 'not a grant journal' across docs/coop/artifacts/*.json returns exactly two source dispositions: route-b.DR-002.preview-disposition.v2.json (P-002-4) and route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v2.json (P-005-2). B-1 is therefore a bounded, one-pass repair — but it is exactly one bound wide, not zero.

shouldFix.measurement: doctor-contract.v4 FC-RO passProperty: '...except for entries whose paths lie inside the declared Operational metadata class root, AND every differing entry inside that root is accounted for by an audit record DOCTOR WROTE ABOUT ITS OWN INVOCATION - or, where that audit record could not be written, by the report's OC-5 outcome.' shouldFix.title: The redaction carve-out inverts file 03's secret scope — it permits redacting handles, when handles are the part that must participate
shouldFix.subjectQuote: SC-OPS journaled/redacted/bounded applies as: secret handles inside records may be redacted; sequence records MUST NOT be dropped or bounded away.
shouldFix.measurement: The preserved V1 secret scope, carried in doctor-contract.v4's governingSources from file 03 lines 41-55: secret VALUES 'are referenced by handles; the HANDLE PARTICIPATES where the exact contract requires it, while the VALUE is excluded from PlanId, evidence digest, diagnostics, and support bundles.' The handle is the non-secret referent that must survive; the value is what is excluded.
shouldFix.whatIsNotWrong: The load-bearing half of the carve-out — sequence records must not be dropped or bounded away — is correct and is exactly the repair CLAUDE-V1-B3's secondary asked for. I am not asking for that half to move.
shouldFix.whyItStillMatters: This clause defines what redaction may touch inside an append-only ordering journal. As written it authorizes removing the handle, which file 03 requires to participate, and says nothing about excluding the value, which is what actually must not be journalled. In a record set whose integrity property is that nothing is dropped, permission to redact the participating referent is the wrong permission to grant.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Invert to match file 03: secret VALUES are excluded from grant-journal records; the HANDLE participates and is not redacted; sequence records must not be dropped or bounded away.

coordinatorNote: One blocker, and it is narrow enough to fix in one editing pass — but I would not treat it as clerical. The question B-1 raises is how many owner-recorded 'not a grant journal' bounds exist. I found two by searching the preview dispositions; the subject found one. Before recording SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL I would want that phrase swept across every owner-recorded disposition, because a supersession that names an incomplete set is worse than one that names none — it looks exhaustive. The four SHOULD-FIX items are all repairs of scope rather than substance: S-1 and S-3 are statements that need widening to match what the artifact already does, S-2 is a two-word inversion, and S-4 is a gate that needs naming. Everything this successor set out to repair, it repaired, and the succession discipline in /basedOn is the strongest I have measured here — I recommend that roster-plus-mechanical-diff pattern be reused. I did not read the other current v2 reviewer, did not edit the subject, file 08, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, and did not commit.
